newsitem.title: UK: Triplex allows Wm Cook offer to lapse.
newsitem.headline: Triplex allows Wm Cook offer to lapse.

text.p: British engineering company Triplex Lloyd said on Wednesday that it would allow its proposed offer for steel castings firm William Cook to lapse at its next closing date of February 7, 1997.

"We correctly identified that William Cook was an undervalued company and would like to have acquired it at a price that we could have justified to our shareholders," Colin Cooke, chairman of Triplex Lloyd said in a statement.

Triplex Lloyd had recently revised its bid offer for William Cook launched in December to 383 pence a share but was pushed aside by a 425 pence-a-share management buyout offer made by Cook's executive chairman Andrew Cook.
Andrew Cook's efforts, backed by venture capital institution Electra Fleming, valued the company at 80 million pounds ($128.3 million).
Triplex had the option to raise its own offer on February 7. By refusing to do so it has virtually left the way open for the management buyout.

In his brief statement Triplex chairman Colin Cooke said; "I am confident that Triplex Lloyd has the management team and the vision to develop its existing businesses for the benefit of its shareholders.
